comments.body:
This is one of those legacy terms that is thown around and rarely discussed in an easy to understand way. For me, I feel when deciding what implementation I want to use I need to consider both security needs and performance trade-offs. If we take the database example you gave you can have it happening at a number of different levels.

1: application level (column as you said above) - this is where sensitive data is encrypted before it reaches the database, but obviously requires care for key management within the application and thus drastically introduces processing overhead and potential complexity.

2: file system (database level example) - here we make use of encrypting the entire database be on the file system or wherever the data for the database resides. This approaches easier as it protects all the data at once but provides less granularity. Often this is the preferred method because it has minimal impact on the application itself. 

There is the hypervisor approach where everything, including the OS and all hypervisor is encrypted. The benefit of this is that the entire virtual machine would be rendered useless if moved outside the insecure environment without the decryption keys.

My question would be on ensuring the requirement is easy to understand, adds vital context as I said above but also offers ease of validating it has been performed, so I'm keen to hear what others think including you @randomstuff
